the design and experimental validation of a low-power multibit Σ Δ ADC for hearing aid application.
the design and evaluation of a multistage ΣΔ modulator for hearing aid applications that achieves high energy efficiency and DR, with the use of nonlinear DACs.

the proposed modulator is a very good solution for the hearing aid application, with a very good trade-off between performance and silicon area.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed modulator achieves the best energy efficiency for the targeted DR and the best area efficiency for the targeted power consumption, which is the most important metric in hearing aids applications.
the modulator proposed achieves the lowest power dissipation and silicon occupation among all ΣΔMs reported so far.
we have designed a low power multibit Σ-Δ modulator with nonlinear feedback DACs, achieving an excellent dynamic range, and with a very small area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nonlinear DACs can be successfully applied to multibit Σ∆Ms, and can be used to achieve a significant DR improvement with no increase in silicon area or power dissipation.
the proposed nonlinear DACs are an effective way to enhance the DR of ΣΔM with low power consumption and area occupation, which is well adapted to hearing aid applications.
